note: CEO letter (first person as Adri, under 300 words, no financial figures) and three asks, from Rypples Engine records only.

sections.letter:
Dear board,

This quarter we agreed with Rypples that plant capital is the one thing holding us back. The pilots are not the limit. Every plant sits in an SPV that we co-own and operate, and nothing earns until a plant is financed and built. Everything below follows from that.

On plant finance, the Finance expert has reviewed our plant-level model, and the unit economics for a standard plant are due this week. Our board-level partner is making introductions to infrastructure funds with water mandates, and I expect the first conversations before the end of the year. What I want from those conversations is a repeatable template, not a one-off deal.

On the pilots, DEWA and Silal remain our two flagship partners. I will confirm where each stands in the pilot section of this pack. The question I keep asking myself is which of them is closest to a multi-plant commitment, because that is what a fund will want to see.

On people, the search for a Head of Projects for MENA is under way, and the scorecard is due this week. Running several sites in the region is still to be proven, and this hire is how we prove it.

The one decision I would like from the board is a clear view on whether Rypples should take a first-loss position in our first plant SPV, so we can tell funds what sits beneath them.

Thank you for the time you give us.

Adri
sections.asks:
1. Decide whether Rypples takes a first-loss position in plant SPV number one. Funds will ask what sits beneath them before they commit.
2. Introduce us to the infrastructure funds with water mandates you know personally. Warm introductions shorten the first plant's financing.
3. Push us on which pilot buyer, DEWA or Silal, can commit to more than one plant. A multi-plant commitment is what turns the template into a pipeline.
